chapter: Central Avenue clubs, Nordskog, Sheffield and Music Town
title: How Sheffield's Blues came to be recorded
summary: At a Hollywood studio another band was playing their planned tune, so Spikes improvised a blues with a knock at the door and Sheffield's catchphrases.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: And so since Sheffield was so much a part of the scene at that time, you dedicated a number to him, huh? You knew everybody...
No, I'll tell you how that happened. We had

rehearsed...uh, I can't think of the song. It was very popular at that time, and we went out to this Hollywood studio to make the record, and when we got there, there was a big white band playing the same thing that we was gonna play--the same tune, so we didn't have anything else rehearsed, and so they said, "Whatta we gonna do, Reb?" I say, "We'll play a bunch of blues, and we'll call it 'Sheffield Blues'," and I say, "We'll start off like the...we'll start to playin', and then there'll be a knock on the door [knocks], and you say, 'Who's there?' [shouts] 'This is Sheffield. Every tub!'" See, that's all on the record, and then they come in and we play a little while and a woman hollers, "Throw it in the sink, Throw't in th' sink. Get rid of it. Throw it in the sink!" That's the whiskey and stuff, see? And it goes on through there, and we play the blues and everything. Then when he gets ready, he say, "Well, let's go-o-o-o," and we finished up, "It had to be yooooooooooooo" [fadeout] [laughs]. I think I got a record around here somewhere of it.
Oh, that'd be fun to hear. So, your record was the first one with the knock on the door--a way before Jack McVea made his hit record.
Oh, yeah. Uh, Little Richard...or what is it?
"Open the Door, Richard." That's interesting. And Sheffield...
